A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLMFP research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. All 57 pages were compared; appendix pages 15–57 are unchanged.

before.justification: v2 reports original planning experiments, baseline comparisons, component ablations, and supplementary evaluations, including Sokoban and paraphrased prompts.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–15 and the iteration-performance analysis.

M1.justification: The LLMFP pipeline, solver use, self-assessment procedure, prompts, and implementation examples are unchanged. Section 3.7 revises the justification for choosing SMT, without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine principal planning tasks, supplementary Sokoban scenarios, and alternative-input evaluations. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Direct, CoT, Code, and Code SMT baselines, model variants, and appendix baselines with explicit optimality instructions.

E3.justification: Task sample counts, model configurations, temperature zero, optimal-rate and success-rate metrics, iteration limits, and supplementary evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, task-specific-example experiment, iteration analysis, failure analyses, formal-input experiment, explicit-optimality comparisons, and paraphrasing robustness test are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests that are added or revised in the other.

E6.justification: Tables 1–15, Figure 3, and reported empirical findings are unchanged. Examples include GPT-4o's 79.1% and 87.5% domain-group optimal-rate averages in Tables 1–2 and its 80.0% Sokoban result in Table 5.

T1.justification: Section 3.7 qualifies the stated theoretical guarantees: SMT can guarantee optimal plans when used for optimization-based planning, and some PDDL planners ensure completeness. This replaces an unconditional optimality statement and a blanket denial of PDDL completeness guarantees. Mathematical formulations and complexity analyses remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: general-purpose zero-shot planning through formalized optimization, strong comparative performance, and effective framework components.

C2.justification: Section 3.7 now explains that many practical PDDL planners prioritize speed and may use incomplete search, while acknowledging complete alternatives. This qualifies the solver-choice rationale. Existing empirical interpretations, failure explanations, and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, solver limits, task inputs, prompts, code examples, runtime and cost information, and the project-page access information are unchanged, including Appendices A.8–A.10.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged, but Section 3.7 moderates the positioning against PDDL planners: their previously categorical completeness disadvantage becomes a qualification about practical search choices, acknowledging planners that ensure completeness.

P1.justification: A localized rewrite expands the solver-guarantee discussion in Section 3.7. The arXiv version/date changes, while section order, the overall narrative, and appendix wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded paragraph causes text reflow across pages 7–13: Section 4.4 starts on page 10 instead of page 9, and the limitations continue onto page 11. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 3.7 reduces overstatement by conditioning the optimality guarantee on optimization-based planning and acknowledging complete PDDL planners. This makes the solver-choice justification more precise and balanced. The benefit is limited because the method, empirical evidence, and complete appendices remain unchanged.
